sections.title: Student Conduct Administration in Higher Education
sections.description: This course will focus on an in-depth understanding of the differing systems that may be available to universities and colleges for student administration. The impact of institutional type on the systems utilized will be explored. This exploration will include for example, institutions described as faith-based, historically, black colleges and universities (HBCU), Hispanic Serving Institutions (HSI), tribal, and two-year institutions. The course will focus on three broad systems of administration. First, the individual student conduct and accountability cases. Second, the differences in approach for student group accountability and third, the alternative resolution options for varying types of incidents. This course will provide a full understanding of due process rights under the law, legal cases impacting conduct cases, a review of current cases, and how due process rights have changed overtime from early 1960s to the present.
